edits.find: Puberty starts the scope, the polyps set the colectomy
edits.with: Known APC carrier: when to start screening and when to operate

edits.find: An APC mutation (autosomal dominant) means hundreds to thousands of adenomas and colon cancer in nearly 100% by age 40. The exam scores two gates. First, screening: annual sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy from age 10–12 (puberty) — not the first-degree-relative rule, not average-risk screening. Second, the operation: prophylactic proctocolectomy is planned for the teens to early 20s, but is indicated at any age for bleeding, large (over 1 cm) or innumerable polyps, or high-grade dysplasia.
edits.with: An APC mutation (autosomal dominant) causes hundreds to thousands of adenomas and colon cancer in nearly 100% by age 40. Screening is annual sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy from age 10–12 (puberty), not the first-degree-relative or average-risk schedule. A prophylactic proctocolectomy is planned for the teens to early 20s and is indicated at any age for bleeding, polyps over 1 cm, innumerable polyps, or high-grade dysplasia.

edits.find: The miss is usually a parameter — the right rung with the wrong number (colonoscopy at 40, or at 10 years before the relative's cancer). Those are the rules for sporadic family history; a known APC carrier is a different pathway. The other tested move is the one after colectomy: upper endoscopy for duodenal and ampullary adenomas, which the colectomy does nothing about.
edits.with: Colonoscopy at 40, or 10 years before the relative's cancer, is the schedule for sporadic family history and does not apply to a known APC carrier. After colectomy, continue upper endoscopy for duodenal and ampullary adenomas.

edits.find: The numbers here belong to a known APC carrier. A first-degree relative with sporadic colon cancer follows a different rule (earlier than average-risk screening, but not annual scoping from puberty), and a Lynch pedigree — few polyps, endometrial cancer in the family — follows a third. Match the pathway before you match the number. Colectomy timing is a plan, not a wait: any of bleeding, polyps over 1 cm, innumerable polyps, or high-grade dysplasia converts "teens to early 20s" into "now."
edits.with: These numbers apply to a known APC carrier. A first-degree relative with sporadic colon cancer follows a different schedule (earlier than average-risk screening, but not annual scoping from puberty), and a Lynch pedigree (few polyps, endometrial cancer in the family) follows a third. Any of bleeding, polyps over 1 cm, innumerable polyps, or high-grade dysplasia means colectomy now rather than in the teens to early 20s.

edits.find: clear the alarm signs, then soften before you instrument
edits.with: Exclude alarm signs, then start an oral laxative before any rectal treatment

edits.find: The stem hands you the mechanism in its chronology: stools were daily and soft until toilet training began, and the pain came before the hardness got worse. That is the withholding cycle — one painful stool teaches the child to hold, holding lets the rectum desiccate the next stool, and the next one hurts more. The anal fissure is the cycle's signature and its accelerant. Everything the examination doesn't show is doing equal work: growth on the 75th percentile with a nontender abdomen and a normal perineum clears the alarm-sign screen, which is what licenses treating rather than investigating. The move is the one that breaks the cycle at its only modifiable point — an oral osmotic laxative to make the next stool painless.
edits.with: Stools were daily and soft until toilet training began, and the pain came before the hardness worsened. This is the withholding cycle: a painful stool leads the child to hold, the rectum desiccates the retained stool, and the next stool hurts more. The anal fissure results from the cycle and worsens it. Growth on the 75th percentile, a nontender abdomen and a normal perineum mean no alarm signs, so treat rather than investigate. Give an oral osmotic laxative to make the next stool painless.

edits.find: the commonest trigger, alongside solid-food and cow's-milk introduction and school entry; it dates the problem to a behavior rather than an anatomy · Previously daily soft stools — normal baseline function excludes a congenital motility defect, which would have declared earlier · Cries and screams with defecation — pain is the engine of withholding, and it is the symptom the laxative is aimed at · Growth tracking at the 75th percentile — clears the growth alarm sign and effectively removes Hirschsprung disease, hypothyroidism and celiac disease · Anal fissure — a complication of hard stools, and the reason a rectal enema is the wrong instrument here · Abdomen firm and mildly distended but nontender — stool load without obstruction; severe distension would be the alarm sign, and this is not it · 24 oz of milk, refuses fruit — the diet is a contributor to modify, not a cause to eliminate · Urinates in the toilet without difficulty — the problem is stool-specific, which argues against a neurologic cause affecting both
edits.with: the commonest trigger, with solid-food and cow's-milk introduction and school entry; points to a behavioral rather than anatomic cause · Previously daily soft stools — normal baseline function excludes a congenital motility defect, which would have presented earlier · Cries and screams with defecation — pain drives withholding and is what the laxative treats · Growth tracking at the 75th percentile — no growth alarm sign; effectively excludes Hirschsprung disease, hypothyroidism and celiac disease · Anal fissure — a complication of hard stools and the reason to avoid a rectal enema · Abdomen firm and mildly distended but nontender — stool load without obstruction; only severe distension is an alarm sign · 24 oz of milk, refuses fruit — diet contributes and should be modified, not eliminated · Urinates in the toilet without difficulty — normal bladder function argues against a neurologic cause

edits.find: Two details invite over-reading in opposite directions. Refusing to eat fruit and the milk volume together read like a dietary indictment, but the stem quietly places the milk at the limit rather than above it, so the diet is a contributor to adjust rather than the answer. And a firm, mildly distended abdomen sounds ominous until you notice the two qualifiers the alarm-sign list actually uses: severe distension, and tenderness. Neither is here. The anal fissure is the most misread finding of all — it is not evidence of an alternative diagnosis, it is the expected complication of the diagnosis you already have, and its only management consequence is to close the rectal route.
edits.with: Refusing to eat fruit and the milk volume suggest a dietary cause, but the milk is at the limit, not above it, so diet is a contributor to adjust. Finding a firm, mildly distended abdomen is not an alarm sign; the alarm signs are severe distension and tenderness, and neither is present. The anal fissure is an expected complication of functional constipation, not evidence of another diagnosis; its only effect on management is to rule out the rectal route.
edits.note: remove dramatic framing and em dash

edits.find: gets an oral osmotic laxative, not a rectal procedure or an image. · Constipation in children is a behavioural cycle with a mechanical consequence; the laxative exists to make the next stool painless so the child stops holding, which is why it runs for months rather than days
edits.with: gets an oral osmotic laxative, not a rectal procedure or imaging. · Childhood constipation is a behavioural cycle with a mechanical consequence; the laxative makes stools painless so the child stops withholding, and it continues for months rather than days

edits.find: The three transitions that generate it are solid food and cow's milk, toilet training, and school entry — a stem that names one is telling you the diagnosis. · An anal fissure is a complication of constipation rather than a competing diagnosis, and it is the reason to disimpact by mouth rather than by rectum. · Hirschsprung disease declares with delayed meconium and poor growth, and fissures are uncommon in it; normal growth with a fissure is functional disease. · Growth is the alarm sign that does the most work — a child tracking a percentile has essentially excluded hypothyroidism, celiac disease and Hirschsprung disease before you order anything. · Enuresis and urinary tract infections are complications of constipation, so a wet child with hard stools gets the bowel treated first.
edits.with: The three common triggers are solid food and cow's milk, toilet training, and school entry; onset at one of them supports the diagnosis. · An anal fissure is a complication of constipation, not a competing diagnosis, and is the reason to disimpact by mouth rather than by rectum. · Hirschsprung disease presents with delayed meconium and poor growth, and fissures are uncommon in it; normal growth with a fissure indicates functional disease. · Growth is the alarm sign that does the most work: a child tracking a percentile has essentially excluded hypothyroidism, celiac disease and Hirschsprung disease. · Enuresis and urinary tract infections are complications of constipation, so in a child with both, treat the bowel first.

edits.find: is the adult mirror of this brief's tier 2 — there the rectal vault is full and the enema is first-line, while here the vault is not and the fissure closes that route. edits.find: When a common condition has a benign screening profile, the examination's normals are the permission to treat, and the alarm-sign list is the only thing that converts treatment into investigation. A complication of the diagnosis is evidence for it rather than against it — but it can still change which instrument you are allowed to use.
edits.with: With no alarm signs and a normal examination, treat; investigate only when an alarm sign is present. A complication of the diagnosis supports it but can still change management, as an anal fissure rules out the rectal route.
